newsitem.title: USA: PLC Systems tumbles after FDA rejection.
newsitem.headline: PLC Systems tumbles after FDA rejection.

text.p: Shares of PLC Systems Inc lost over half their value on Tuesday following a U.S. Food and Drug Administration panel's recommendation Monday that the FDA reject the company's Heart Laser System.
Shares were trading at 11-3/8, down 56 percent from Monday's close of 25-10/16.

The FDA advisory committee voted nine to two to reject PLC's system for treatment of patients with chronic chest pain who do not respond to angioplasty or coronary artery bypass surgery. It said PLC presented incomplete trial data.
"This is a major blow. It is their (PLC's) one and only business," said Alexander Arrow, a medical devices anayst for Wedbush Morgan Securities.

Arrow said the FDA panel's decision should be a cautionary tale to other companies seeking approval for similar devices, which drill tiny holes into the heart to restore blood flow to damaged heart tissue.
"It will send a message to the others that in order to get approval they have to have thorough data," he said.
CardioGenesis Corp of Sunnyvale, Calif., which is expected to seek FDA approval of a different form of the laser early next year, was up 1/16 to 11.

Eclipse Surgical Technologies Inc, also of Sunnyvale, recently applied to the FDA for approval of its laser. It received approval last December to market the laser in the European Community. Its shares were off 3/8 to 7-7/8.

Another medical products analyst noted the FDA panel had encouraged PLC Systems to re-submit its application along with missing data on about 40 percent of the patients who underwent its clinical trials.
"But who knows how long that will take? It could be six months or years before they track down the data and come back. It's going to be difficult for them," the analyst said.
